title: What is known about 1RB1RF_1LC0RB_1RD0LC_1LE1RA_0RC1LB_---1RE
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB1RF_1LC0RB_1RD0LC_1LE1RA_0RC1LB_---1RE.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state machine halts from blank tape. This page records what is established about it, sorted by what each result rests on. Only a first analysis has been done: the macro rules are not yet known.
The tape is blocks of 1s, mostly 1^3 on the left and 1^3 or 1^4 on the right, separated by one, two or more 0s. Both ends grow like the logarithm of the step count.
verdict: The question is open. No halt in the first 1010 steps (C simulator); the macro configuration and its rules are not yet known.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F0); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>10</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/tmrun.c runs 1010 steps from blank tape without a halt; at the end the tape holds 1,224 ones.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 1,538 cells have been visited and 949 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Where a halt can be
claims.text: A closed tape language of windows of 5 cells (tools/py/bbtools/ctl.py, closure checked by the script, not by Lean) contains every configuration reachable from blank tape, and its only halting configurations have F reading a 0 with three 1s just left of the head (1 1 1 F>0).

claims.title: Not decided by n-gram CPS up to width 14
claims.text: The n-gram Closed Position Set decider (tools/c/ngramcps.c) with equal widths 4, 6, 8, 10, 12 and 14, plain and with the fixed-length (1) and LRU history augmentations, either reaches a halting local configuration (UNKNOWN) or stops at 3·107 local configurations: it does not prove non-halting at these settings.

claims.title: Growth shape: exp/exp
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.099). Right of the start it grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.089).

claims.title: The blocks
claims.text: At the last left records before 109: C>0 0^2 1^3 0^2 1^3 0 1^3 0^2 1^3 0 1^3 0^2 1 0^2 ...; at the right: ... 1^3 0 1^4 0 1^4 0 1^4 0 1^4 ..., with gaps of one, two, four or five 0s. Hundreds of blocks, changing at many places between visits to the ends.

claims.title: The ends grow three cells at a time
claims.text: In snapshots of the leftmost 60 cells taken whenever they change (4,922 snapshots in 109 steps), the left end moved 176 times, every time by exactly 3 cells. At the 312 visits to the right end (the head arriving after being more than 50 cells away) in 109 steps it had grown by 3 cells 294 times. The left end is made of words 1110, 11100 and 1100, with a marker 0000 that travels along it; what they encode is not known.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. The macro configuration family has not been found.

explainer.lede: This machine fills its tape with short blocks of 1s, mostly three or four long, and both ends of the tape grow like the logarithm of the step count, the mark of counters. Its macro rules have not been worked out yet. It has run 10<sup>10</sup> steps without halting.

facts.text: No halt in the C simulator.
No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.
The growth shape of the two sides of the tape (see below).

sections.heading: Blocks of three and four
html: The tape is blocks of 1s, mostly 1^3 on the left and 1^3 or 1^4 on the right, separated by gaps of one, two, four or five 0s. For example, at step 920,800,871 the left end reads C>0 0^2 1^3 0^2 1^3 0 1^3 0^2 1^3 0 1^3 0^2 1 0^2 1^3 0 ..., and the right end has long runs (1^4 0)^n.

Both ends grow like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell at an end costs a roughly constant factor more time, as for a counter. Between two visits to an end many blocks change, so the counter, if it is one, has a more complicated set of digits than binary.

sections.heading: Where a halt could happen
html: The machine stops when F reads a 0. A closed tape language with windows of 5 cells, which contains every configuration reachable from blank tape, adds that the three cells left of the head must be 1s: 1 1 1 F>0.

sections.heading: What is not known
html: Not known: the digits of the counter (which words play the part of digits), the carry rule, and whether a carry can ever produce 1 1 1 F>0.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.099). Right of the start it grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.089).
After 109 steps the tape spans 1,538 cells (498 left of the start, 901 right), with a density of 1s of 0.617.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

family: Counter-like growth on both sides (exp/exp; structure not yet found)
summary: Blocks of 1s (mostly 1^3 and 1^4) separated by 0s, changing like counters on both sides; no halt in 10^10 steps; macro rules not yet found.
